summary.claim: Only this bounded selection; no native aggregate or release qualification.

limits: Two complete existing test files retain all 29 cases and their original assertions. The editor file has 12 cases and a 480-second wrapper bound; core receive has 17 and a 300-second bound. Individual non-generated limits stay 45/40 seconds and generated limits 200/180 seconds respectively. Owned browser startup remains 15 seconds and drain grace five seconds. Product code, wrappers, mutation bodies, shared browser owner and census are unchanged. Only the historical-reader git show receives finite 5000-ms/2-MiB bounds.

The core historical control executes promotionRecord.ts at 8378596; its exact reference/revision/path/hash is pinned in that file's receipt and checked before launch/reuse and after execution. The existing historical input allowlist and owner controls cover this path; no new locator grammar or owner code was needed. Rejection by this composite old-reader fixture and the v8-to-v9 activation boundary do not revive support for the retired v8 app.

The promotion fixture registers cleanup before setup, borrows a validated owned loopback CDP endpoint, and creates synthetic contexts, credential/recovery fixtures and temporary loopback Account service/SQLite files. Services are used for setup/authority; inbound pages and acceptance proofs come from the independent Node/OpenSSL oracle, not a service delivery route. Inbound envelopes use separate browser framing and current WebCrypto under synthetic member keys, including deliberate 256-update adversarial input. Core generated histories share one browser context/service but create distinct workspaces; editor histories create and promptly close separate contexts. Outer test cleanup closes services/connections and the stage owner drains Chromium.

Core directed tests compare atomic original content/evidence, duplicate/no-outbound capture, compaction and expired retained proof replay; four explicit renderer deaths cover receive and v9 activation before/after commit. Other cases remove content/events, corrupt ciphertext, reauthenticate invalid service-page/baseline evidence under valid local AEAD/witness, preserve pending Yjs originals until a later dependency, retain conflict, drain held crypto before releasing the slot, reject oversized batches before reservation, abort/retry a 255-update-plus-event transaction and reject authority changed during sealing.

Core controls separately omit reuse and fallback coverage checks and require rejection to remain; only omitting both admits missing content. Witness omission resets received progress, split-content mutation commits evidence without its content and is detected by immediate/cold readback, and stored-page verification omission admits a locally reauthenticated invalid service signature. These are distinct observations, not a generic nonzero-exit oracle.

Twelve core generated histories retain seed 9182026 and numRuns:12, with ordinary fast-check shrinking and the existing 180-second test deadline. Each history has one to three receive operations with before/after/no commit cut and optional compaction/cold reopen. Cursor checks occur at each step and after crash/retry; final cold content replay is compared with independent expected text. This is not an exact original-byte comparison after every action. The twelve-history population and test bound are unchanged.

Ordered editor cases require remote publication after durable commit with no local capsule, undo or outgoing event; queued Local input is prepared only after remote publication. They cover two receive commit crashes, malformed/bad-signature pages, retained conflict with continued Local editing, pending structs/deletes through compaction, storage-pressure suffix discard, held committed receive during close with a second page competing for the same slot, and observer-triggered close followed by complete cold replay. Early-publication and local-relabel mutations must expose the prohibited visible text or extra source capsule. The early-publication control also crashes its renderer.

Ten editor generated histories retain seed 9202026, numRuns:10, endOnFailure:true and the 200-second case deadline. Three to six actions draw from receive/local/duplicate/invalid/compact/restart. Text, cursor and local source counts are compared after each action, with text/source counts compared after final reopen. There is no explicit all-action-coverage assertion, and a duplicate action before the first receive is a no-op. Do not describe this as a generated network-fault campaign.

Reopen means a new page in the same browser context; CDP Page.crash is renderer death, not a browser-process crash, power loss or a separate device. Storage failures and authority/ciphertext changes are deliberate synthetic native-boundary injections. Optional ACCOUNT_REPORT_DIR exports remain disabled, so their exact saved-output postconditions, original wrapper ordering and prerequisites remain separate unresolved obligations.

All 92 pure runner checks pass. Unchanged 23 Node owner, five Vitest-process and twelve native-owner checks retain pinned earlier evidence rather than new execution. The ledger phase's first expected-positive historical service-path orphan classification remains unresolved despite subsequent passes; this phase establishes no fix.

All 179 prior general contracts / 1473 case identities and six retired-v8 exclusions remain unchanged. The full frozen source/dependency/browser archives are retained locally with hashes here; subsequent documentation changes do not make this an immutable aggregate. The preceding sync/composition phase is signed and verified. Personal profiles/services/builds/recovery/factors, earlier vectors/evidence/debts/signing backups, unrelated root done-space and L-2 remain untouched.

Node execution passed with less than three seconds of margin against the existing file deadline. Stage elapsed also includes preparation/drain work. Loaded-host reliability remains unqualified; the passing run does not justify a deadline change.
